newsitem.title: UK: CORTECS UP ON PRELIMINARY DRUG TRIAL RESULT.
newsitem.headline: CORTECS UP ON PRELIMINARY DRUG TRIAL RESULT.

text.p: Shares in Anglo-Australian pharmaceutical company Cortecs International Ltd hit a two-month high on Tuesday after the firm released positive preliminary results for its bronchitis drug trial.
By 0845 GMT the shares were trading up 20-1/2 pence at 2.40 pounds.
The shares had hit a high of 2.50 stg earlier, levels not seen since May 14.
One analyst attributed the stock's rise to the test results, which the company said were even better than expected.
The drug, called Pseudostat, was tested on 91 patients who had a history of two or more acute attacks of bronchitis a year.
Results showed the number of infections in people who did not take the drug was approximately 10 times higher than those who took Pseudostat.
But analysts said the preliminary results were not enough in themselves and they would have to wait for fuller statistics before they could make up their mind on the drug.
"At first sight the data looks impressive but it is preliminary," said one analyst who did not want to be named.
Another analyst said drug shares had been subdued recently and this news, despite being preliminary, was something for the market to get its teeth into.
"The sector has been looking for some good news and anything exciting tends to get seized upon," the analyst said. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
